recentItems.title: TRUMP’S ULTIMATUM FOILED: Kyiv resumes strikes on Russia — jets are on fire!
recentItems.description:
"Neptune" missiles struck Borisoglebsk: the Navy reported six Su-34M jets destroyed. Ukraine is resuming attacks on Russian oil refineries, while a fire at an oil terminal continues for a fifth straight day. Starlink restrictions disrupted Armed Forces of Ukraine missions, prompting Thom Tillis to demand an investigation into Pentagon actions. Meanwhile, Russia launched over 850 more drones, as the US considers easing sanctions on the shadow fleet and unfreezing part of Russian assets. This edition also covers disruptions at Moscow airports and Operation "Vivaldi": 101 km² reclaimed during the fourth stage, 277 km² in total. How do the Armed Forces of Ukraine's successes change the front-line situation, and why is Kyiv calling on partners to strengthen air defense?

recentItems.title: THE END OF THE 'CEASEFIRE'? Zelenskyy gives green light. Missiles destroy Russian airbase
recentItems.description:
Four Su-34s destroyed, two damaged: Ukrainian "Neptune" missiles hit the Borisoglebsk airfield. Volodymyr Zelenskyy released a satellite image and stated that the aircraft were being prepared for new attacks on Ukraine. Kyiv will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries, while the EU offers the secure Govsatcom satellite network to reduce reliance on Starlink. In Brussels, Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Mark Rutte discuss air defense missiles and ammunition for F-16s. Estonia will provide 10 million euros for weapons via PURL. The report also covers over 850 Russian drones in a single day and strengthened protection for Black Sea shipping, as Romania and Bulgaria agree to counter drone threats.

recentItems.title: Ukraine "switches off" Russian internet: drones burn down $1 BILLION Sberbank data center!
recentItems.description:
Three Yandex data centers stopped operating following Ukrainian strikes, causing over 80 digital services to fail. A major Sberbank data center was also hit, while the fate of Yandex’s three supercomputers remains unknown. The Armed Forces of Ukraine destroyed a 96L6 radar and a Buk-M3 system valued at approximately $95 million. According to General Staff data, Russia lost 6,390 troops killed and wounded, along with 194 artillery systems, in just four days. In Russian Losses: the strike on a Mi-28 helicopter, attacks on an Iskander repair base and an oil hub in the Samara region, plummeting Russian oil and gas revenues, and Operation "Vivaldi," which returned 277 km² to Ukrainian control. Counting the damages.
